title: Stop.
paragraphs:
You’re not tired because life is heavy…
You’re tired because you’re trying to control what was never yours to carry.
And here’s the part you don’t say out loud:

You trust God…
but still grip everything like it all depends on you.

You say “Lord, I surrender”—
but your hands are still clenched.
And deep down… you know it.

This is a quiet war between your need for control
and God’s call to trust.

You check your phone again.
You replay the conversation.
You overthink the future like you can out-strategize uncertainty.
Let me say something that might shake you:

Worry is not just emotion.
It’s misplaced worship.

You’re giving your attention, your energy, your focus…
to things that cannot save you.

You’re bowing—not with your knees,
but with your thoughts.

Exhaustion.
Fear.
A heart that never rests.
Jesus didn’t stay silent about this.
He stepped right into your anxiety and said:
“Can any one of you by worrying add a single hour to your life?” — Matthew 6:27
You think worrying gives you control.
But Jesus exposes it for what it really is:
“Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life…” — Matthew 6:25

Some scholars interpret this passage as Jesus confronting not just anxiety,
but a deeper issue—

A heart that says it trusts God…
but lives like everything depends on itself.

“I need to figure this out.”
“I can’t let this fall apart.”
“I have to stay in control.”
But Scripture cuts through that illusion:
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
And here’s where it gets real.
Your worry isn’t just draining you.
You don’t fully trust Him yet.
And that’s where the Gospel steps in.
Because you’re not the first person to struggle with this.
Humanity has always tried to take control.

From the garden of Eden—
when we reached for what God didn’t give—

to right now…
scrolling, stressing, striving.
Sin at its core is this:
A life built on unstable ground.
But God didn’t leave you there.
Jesus didn’t come to make you a better worrier.
He came to set you free.

Free from sin.
Free from fear.
Free from the crushing burden of trying to be your own savior.
Jesus took everything you’re trying to control.

Your past.
Your failures.
Your unknown future.
“Cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you.” — 1 Peter 5:7

The work you’re trying to do…
Jesus already completed.
You don’t have to hold everything together.
Because He already held it on the cross.

Proving that even death…
even your worst-case scenario…
So what are you really afraid of?
It was never yours to secure.
Even your failure can’t cancel God’s grace.
You don’t fight worry by trying harder.
You fight it by surrendering deeper.
You don’t silence anxiety by gaining control.
You silence it by trusting Christ.
The relationship you’re afraid will break?
The opportunity you’re scared to lose?
The version of your life you’re desperately trying to preserve?
Because peace doesn’t come from control.
“You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on You, because he trusts in You.” — Isaiah 26:3
Say it out loud if you have to:
Let go of the illusion that you were ever in control.
And if you’ve never truly surrendered your life to Jesus—

not just your problems,
but your entire self—
Stop trying to be your own god.
And trust the One who died and rose for you.
Because salvation is not found in control.
He is not asking you to fix your life.
He is asking you to give it.
So here’s what I want you to do:

If this pierced something in you…
don’t ignore it.
Come back when the anxiety tries to return.
And the truth has a name:
From control to surrender — because Jesus already holds it all.
